video_title: Steph Curry’s Extension, Jimmy Butler’s Return and Where is Kristaps Porzingis?!

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Kristaps Porzingis out indefinitely with a health issue
quotes.excerpt: Kristaps Porzingis I got a call last night. He's dealing with a health issue, he's out indefinitely.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: I told you Mike Dunleavy was talking at 8:00. At 7:59, you get the Raymond Ridder update of, hey, Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody are making progress, they're doing light on-court activities, and we'll announce more in a few weeks about their progress. And then Dunleavy takes the mic. That was expected. And then Dunleavy takes the mic and says, oh, also, Kristaps Porzingis, I got a call last night. He's dealing with a health issue, he's out indefinitely.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Not going to Hawaii. That takes him out of the first five practices and the first preseason game, which is in Honolulu. That's all they're saying. Dunleavy even said, hey, I'm not marking him out to start the season. But obviously, for this to be the first thing you hear at 8:01 a.m. on media day, with the context of what he's missed 90 games over the last two years, not all because of the health issues, but a large chunk of it.

quotes.speaker: Tim Bontemps
quotes.summary_phrase: Kristaps Porzingis's contract reflects his frequent injury absences
quotes.excerpt: This is why Porzingis is on a contract that has only $3 million guaranteed next year.
quotes.quote: This is why Porzingis is on a contract that has only $3 million guaranteed next year. He's impactful when he's on the floor, but he's just not on the floor that often for a variety of medical reasons.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Warriors' roster depth concerns entering training camp
quotes.excerpt: They now, at least entering training camp right now, don't have three starters.
quotes.quote: This is why they signed the contract they did, which is two years, $40 million, but the second year only has $3 million guaranteed. They can get out of it next summer and open up more cap space. But if we are literally talking about the Warriors this season and their outlook, they now, at least entering training camp right now, don't have three starters. Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody out until mid-season probably, and then we'll see on Kristaps Porzingis. These are three of their six most important players.

quotes.speaker: Tim Bontemps
quotes.summary_phrase: Warriors' outlook limited to a play-in team
quotes.excerpt: It's just extremely difficult to envision any scenario that results in the Warriors being anything more than a cute play-in team.
quotes.quote: It's just extremely difficult to envision any scenario that results in the Warriors being anything more than a cute play-in team this year. I guess some kind of blockbuster deal can fall out of the sky. If Anthony Davis arrives there, I don't even know if that bumps them into the top six in the West. Any hope I think for the Warriors to return to competitive relevance will be at least two transaction cycles of the trade deadline and the summer away, at least.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen Curry's contract extension details and player option
quotes.excerpt: What it really was was one year, $55.7 million.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: What it really was was one year, $55.7 million. And part of the benefit bonus of Steph taking it is the player option he got on the second year. He can scrap that up and get to his max if needed.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Steph gave them a break, but Steph ain't in the mood to leave a lot of money on the old table, which I don't blame him for 100% to be clear.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Warriors considered waiting to sign Stephen Curry's extension
quotes.excerpt: One of the options Steph was contemplating was literally just not signing anything until later.
quotes.quote: Mike Dunleavy and Steph and Jeff Austin, they all went through various scenarios, which includes max flexibility. One of the options Steph was contemplating was literally just not signing anything until later in the season or potentially June, July of next year, which would have been maximum type flexibility because they would have really been able to maneuver Steph's contract down to the dollar that they knew they needed later. Steph, at the end of the day, who wanted security, he's turning 39 this year, his knee, all that, just said, okay, I'll give you $10 million back.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Jimmy Butler's knee recovery and testing numbers
quotes.excerpt: My testing numbers are staggering. They're off the charts. I'm ahead, so they say.
quotes.quote: He was talking about his knee, and he's been doing strengthening tests. He said, my testing numbers are staggering. They're off the charts. I'm ahead, so they say. He's going to be off to the side doing individual work in Hawaii. He's weeks, potentially a month away from contact work.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.excerpt: They're both sides are expressing optimism. They're still talking. October 19th is obviously the deadline.
quotes.quote: They're both sides are expressing optimism. They're still talking. October 19th is obviously the deadline. I wish I had the exact number up, the cap hold is important here. His cap hold next year is roughly $17.5 million. As protective and down to the dollar as we've seen the Warriors are about their future flexibility, I don't imagine they're going to want on an extension with Podziemski to go too much beyond that cap hold.
